hint.text:
Commas cannot be used to separate two main clauses, unless there is already a coordinating conjunction in place.

Semi-colons can be used to separate two main clauses.

Because of this, we say that semi-colons are stronger than commas.

instruction.text: Decide whether the punctuation in this sentence is correct.

atoms.a: We’re going to the beach later today, don’t forget to pack the sun cream.

end.text: This sentence contains two main clauses, so should be separated by a semi-colon. Commas can’t be used between two main clauses if there is not already a coordinating conjunction in place.

atoms.a: I love cats, and I hope to own one in the future.
The sky is so blue today; the clouds disappeared a couple of hours ago.
I want to go swimming in the sea; yet the water looks freezing.

end.text: This sentence contains a main clause and a coordinate conjunction, and so it should be separated by a comma.

atoms.b: We left school early yesterday((++; --,))today is the first day of the holidays.
atoms.sound: We left school early yesterday; today is the first day of the holidays.

atoms.b: My neighbours invited me to their garden party tomorrow((--; ++,))so I’ll have to cancel the plans with my sister.
atoms.sound: My neighbours invited me to their garden party tomorrow, so I’ll have to cancel the plans with my sister.

atoms.b: I wanted to turn the music down((--; ++,))but I can’t remember where I put my phone.
atoms.sound: I wanted to turn the music down, but I can’t remember where I put my phone.

atoms.b: This new blanket is so soft((++; --,))I just found our pets hiding underneath.
atoms.sound: This new blanket is so soft; I just found our pets hiding underneath
